items.message: The sandbox-refusal test for CommandTest, CommandValidate, CommandBuild, and CommandRun patches `sandbox.runtime` to return None, but the test never actually runs the adapters through code that calls `_refused`. It asserts `outcome.status is Status.BLOCKED`, which is the right assertion — but it would be worth confirming the test actually reaches `_refused` in `command.py` rather than being blocked earlier (e.g. before the sandbox is even invoked). This is not a clear defect, but the path throug…[truncated]

The `not_a_verdict` test asserts `passed.findings[0].id == 'cost.budget_exceeded'` but does not assert `passed.status is Status.BLOCKED` directly after checking `passed is not None` — it does check `passed.status is Status.BLOCKED` in the same assertion line, so this is fine. No gap here.

The test `test_a_pack_refused_by_a_control_is_not_a_pack_that_broke` asserts only that `REFUSED != ERRORED` — that the two string constants differ. It does not assert that a `_review_case` call on a BLOCKED outcome actually returns a `CaseResult` with `state=REFUSED`. The new branch in `trial.py` at line 194 is the thing the test is described as covering, but the test would pass with the branch reverted. A test asserting `result.state == REFUSED` when `outcome.status is Status.BLOCKED` would be …[truncated]

The `test_a_resolver_that_succeeded_with_no_files_is_a_failed_backport` test asserts `outcome.status is Status.FAILED` but does not assert that `not_a_verdict` / `_resolver_stopped` was NOT invoked — i.e. it does not confirm the SUCCEEDED path falls through correctly to `_conflict_outcome`. Given that `_resolver_stopped` returns `None` for SUCCEEDED, this works, but a passing assertion on `outcome.reason == 'backport.conflict'` (the hard-coded value in `_conflict_outcome`) would close the loop.
